operations.evidence: The 31 March 2025 neighbourhood policing baseline was 17,175 FTE officers and PCSOs.
The baseline is a programme measure and excludes parcel-level deployment information.
There were 20,989 FTE personnel in neighbourhood policing roles or in training for such roles at 31 March 2026.
The total combines deployed and training personnel and cannot indicate exact-address coverage.
The neighbourhood policing total included 14,599 FTE police officers, of whom 350 FTE were in training.
Personnel in training may not yet be operationally deployed, so the figure is not parcel evidence.
The neighbourhood policing total included 6,390 FTE PCSOs, of whom 122 FTE were in training.
Training and in-post counts cannot be treated as local presence at a property.
Neighbourhood policing personnel grew by 3,814 FTE, or 22.2%, above the March 2025 baseline.
Programme growth is an aggregate and does not map personnel to individual parcels.
Police officers accounted for 3,494 FTE, or 91.6%, of neighbourhood policing growth.
The share of programme growth does not establish local service outcomes.
PCSOs accounted for 319 FTE, or 8.4%, of neighbourhood policing growth.
The aggregate share cannot identify the location or timing of deployment.
The updated year-one neighbourhood policing growth target was 3,011 FTE.
A programme target is not evidence that any specific parcel received additional policing.
Total neighbourhood policing growth reached 126.7% of the updated year-one target.
Target achievement does not demonstrate uniform deployment or local safety effects.
Neighbourhood police officer growth reached 133.7% of the officer target.
An aggregate target ratio cannot be translated into a parcel-level candidate.
Neighbourhood PCSO growth reached 80.6% of the PCSO target.
The programme ratio does not measure service coverage around a property.
Neighbourhood policing programme figures exclude employees on long-term absence.
The exclusion means the figures are not identical to all workforce totals and require cautious comparison.
Neighbourhood policing programme figures exclude British Transport Police.
The scope exclusion prevents treating the figures as all-policing coverage for every location.
There were 20,517 FTE officers and PCSOs recorded in neighbourhood policing roles excluding those still in training.
A role snapshot does not show shift patterns, patrol intensity or parcel-level presence.
Of personnel in neighbourhood policing roles excluding trainees, 1,206 FTE, or 5.9%, were standard direct recruits since April 2025.
Recruitment route does not indicate effectiveness or risk at an address.
There were 472 FTE direct-recruit officers, equal to 3.3% of neighbourhood police officers in role.
The category is a workforce characteristic, not local incident evidence.
There were 734 FTE direct-recruit PCSOs, equal to 11.7% of neighbourhood PCSOs in role.
The category cannot be spatially attributed to a parcel.
A 27.7% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had one to less than five years of service.
Experience distribution is an aggregate workforce measure and not a local safety outcome.
A 28.5% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had five to less than ten years of service.
Service-band shares cannot identify capability at a specific address.
A 5.8% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had less than one year of service.
A national experience share is not parcel-level evidence.
A 62.1% share of neighbourhood officers and PCSOs had less than ten years of service, compared with 53.6% across all officers and PCSOs.
The comparison is descriptive and does not measure operational quality at a location.
A 11.2% share of neighbourhood personnel had 20 to less than 25 years of service, compared with 16.7% across all officers and PCSOs.
Experience-band differences cannot be converted into a parcel risk score.
A 3.3% share of neighbourhood personnel had 25 to less than 30 years of service, compared with 6.9% across all officers and PCSOs.
The aggregate comparison gives no exact-address coverage evidence.
Constables accounted for 80.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
Rank composition is organisational information and not a local outcome measure.
Sergeants accounted for 15.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
Rank share cannot identify supervision or patrol conditions at a parcel.
Inspectors accounted for 4.2% of neighbourhood police officers.
The national proportion cannot establish local command availability.
Chief inspectors accounted for 0.3% of neighbourhood police officers.
The rank proportion is not parcel-level public-safety evidence.
Superintendents accounted for 0.04% of neighbourhood police officers.
A very small national rank share cannot support exact-address inference.
No neighbourhood police officers were recorded at chief superintendent or chief officer rank.
The absence reflects function coding and does not imply missing local command arrangements.
There were 43,525 police officers with less than five years of service, equal to 29.4% of officers on a headcount basis.
Length-of-service data are workforce characteristics, not parcel safety measures.
